name: Self-model discovery (SMD): learning principles found inside a recorded model of the learner's own acquisition landscape, with the model refit by every principle that real runs adopt
core_idea: The system records, from real constructions on the training pools of source categories, how its own fixed linear policy (generation 0's score and pick programs) scores as a function of its constants: a table from block-normalised theta directions to the (hard, soft) cost key of every problem. It then uses that table as a simulator of its own acquisition. Any design-o learning principle (the init/propose/update programs, pop, batch, holdback, select and the starting constants) can be run there for about 0.5 CPU-s, against about 100 CPU-s for one candidate evaluation in design o's kernel screening. Discovery uses design o's discoverer, whose edit weights are learned by the current parent's own principle; it tries about 64 candidates per step in the simulator. Only the best simulated candidate of each 16-step generation goes to a real kernel confirmation (16 new seeds x 4 categories, paired), and only that real result can adopt a candidate. An adopted principle then changes how the next candidates are generated (it learns the discoverer's weights), how they are evaluated (the table is refit with real constructions wherever the adopted principle's simulated runs go) and where they start from. Every product is an ordinary design-o version, so no file pinned by registration_o changes, including the kernel and designs.py.
why_it_beats_the_measured_limit:
The measured limit (design o): one step costs 400-800 CPU-s for 6 candidates. A screened candidate's value predicts its promotion value with a correlation of 0.10. A 6,000 CPU-s lineage gets about 10 steps. The acceptance rule needs a mean of at least 0.0137 over 16 pairs (paired sd 0.021, t >= 2.6), and 0 of 4 confirmations passed. Confirmed candidates were worth +0.0089 on the discovery seeds and +0.0012 on fresh seeds. True effects among edits that do not break the mechanism are small: cell means range from -0.040 to +0.011, and positive screeners confirm at about +0.001.

(1) Evaluation. A candidate's simulated value is the mean paired difference from its parent over 48 simulated acquisitions (12 per category, common random numbers). The estimated cost is about 0.5 CPU-s per candidate (vector-machine programs plus a 16 x 4,000 x 10 nearest-neighbour search per round), to be measured in development. That gives 64 candidates per step and about 80 steps, or about 5,000 candidate evaluations per lineage instead of about 60. Noise then stops being the limit. The limit becomes fidelity rho: the rank correlation between a candidate's simulated value and its real paired effect. Rho is measured before registration (D4) and in the run (H3).

(2) The real gate. Knapsack is dropped (zero signal) and bin packing added. With 16 seeds x 4 categories and per-category paired sd 0.039 (QAP), 0.021 (job shop), 0.006 (p-median) and about 0.005 (bin packing), the stratified SE is 0.0028. The rule accepts if z >= 2.33 and the mean is >= 0.004. The smallest accepted mean is 0.0065, half of 0.0137. Power is 0.18 at an effect of 0.004, 0.42 at 0.006, 0.70 at 0.008, 0.89 at 0.010 and 0.99 at 0.013. One confirmation costs about 1,630 CPU-s (about 51 CPU-s per mechanism-seed over the four categories, both sides). False acceptance is 1% per confirmation, to be null-calibrated with the noise stub used for registration_o, and at most 5% per lineage of 5 confirmations.

(3) Expected acceptances. Assume real effects among principle and scalar edits have mean -0.002 and sd 0.006. The top of about 1,000 simulated candidates per generation then has an expected real effect of rho x 3.2 x 0.006 - 0.002:
* rho 0.7: +0.0114, P(accept) 0.96;
* rho 0.5: +0.0076, P(accept) 0.65;
* rho 0.3: +0.0038, P(accept) 0.16;
* rho 0: P(accept) about 0.001, so only false acceptances.

Over about 5 confirmations per lineage, with headroom shrinking after each acceptance, that is about 1.6 acceptances per lineage at rho 0.5, 0.6 at rho 0.3 and 0.05 at rho 0. A real-only arm with the same gate gets about 0.3: its promoted best is worth about +0.001 to +0.004.

(4) Winner's curse. Selection happens in the simulator, and the confirmation seeds are used by nothing else, so a confirmed mean is an unbiased estimate on these four categories.

(5) Held-out. Four fresh categories x 24 seeds, fixed-category paired mean, one-sided alpha 0.025. At paired sd 0.03 the SE is 0.0031: power 0.90 for 0.01 and 0.37 for 0.005. At sd 0.04 the power is 0.69 and 0.23.

What it cannot beat: category heterogeneity (cross-category correlation of effects about 0). An effect specific to the four source landscapes will show as a null on held-out. The category-resampled statistic of registration_o is not powered at all with four categories. The held-out recursion contrast (W-rec vs W-frozen) is powered only above about 0.008; its powered test is the paired swap inside the simulator.
recursion:
There are three channels, each with its own control.

* **Generation.** As in design o, the discoverer's weights over the W cells are learned by the current parent's own init/propose/update programs (design_o.Acquirer over the weight vector, simulated values as fitness). The W cells are the init/propose/update edits, the pop, batch, holdback and select scalars, and theta/perturb. With 64 candidates per step and about 80 steps, that principle gets about 80 updates per lineage instead of about 10. An adopted principle takes over: the discoverer is rebuilt on it from the current weights.
* **Evaluation.** After each adoption, 100 simulated acquisitions per category are run with the adopted mechanism. Every proposed theta whose nearest table neighbour is farther than REFIT_RADIUS is queued, and up to 500 per category are constructed for real on the table problems and added to the table, with their CPU charged to the lineage. Later candidates are edits of the adopted mechanism and search where it searches, so they are scored on a table its own behaviour shaped.
* **Improvement.** The adopted mechanism's scalars and starting constants define its descendants' simulated acquisitions and the parent side of every paired simulated comparison.

Controls:
* W-frozen: generation 0's principle always learns the weights, with the same refits. It isolates generation.
* W-static: W-rec with no refit. It isolates evaluation.
* W-shuffled: keys permuted across theta within each problem's column. It is the negative control for the evaluator and an empirical check of the gate's false acceptance.
* Paired swap in the simulator: 24 replicate pairs of lineages from generation 0 at equal simulated CPU, with the discoverer's principle taken from W-rec's final in one and from generation 0 in the other. Each replicate's best is scored on an independent table of 20 other problems per category, and the top 3 pairs are checked by real runs on part B. It isolates the effect of a discovered principle on discovery itself.
* Held-out W-rec - W-frozen@matched and W-rec - W-static@matched are the real versions; they are powered only above about 0.008.

If W-rec never adopts a principle change, W-rec and W-frozen are identical. The recursion is then recorded as not exercised, not as a null.
mechanism_changes:
Unchanged: rsi6/kernel, learner/design_o.py, learner/designs.py, open/discovery.py, open/edits.py, and every other file pinned by registration_o (they are imported, never edited). The products are design-o versions, run through the pinned dispatch, so the running open experiment's per-stage file checks are not disturbed. W cannot share a ledger with that experiment while it writes (single writer), so it runs after it.

New files:
* rsi6/world/__init__.py.
* rsi6/world/landscape.py:
  * record(categories, n_theta, n_problems, seed) builds problems from training-pool instances only (environments.load(c).problem(i, Meter, relabel, training=True), wrapped by kernel.problem.view, never the kernel's fresh split). It never calls env.score or env.reference. It samples theta from a registered plan: generation 0's prior plus N(0, s^2) for s in {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}, and points along generation 0's own trajectories. It runs design_o.construct and stores an npz with the theta table, block-normalised directions (score block theta0-6 and pick block theta7-9; argmax is invariant to positive scaling of each block), the (hard, soft) keys per theta and problem, the construction units per problem and the generation-0 key, plus a ledger record with digests and measured CPU.
  * refit(table, thetas) adds rows.
* rsi6/world/simulator.py:
  * simulate(mechanism, table, task, seed) mirrors OpenLearner._acquire_open: the same meter arithmetic (limit 40 x the sum of construction units, reserve 3 x the check cost, n_vars*n_opts + n_vars + 1 per construction), the same three random streams, design_o.Acquirer and design_o._fitness unchanged, the best_of_3 held-back check, and k-NN surrogate keys (k = 3, distance-weighted).
  * The internal gain proxy is the mean, over fresh-proxy table problems, of the lexicographic relative improvement of the chosen theta over the start theta.
  * value(candidate, parent, tasks) is the mean paired difference over 48 tasks.
* rsi6/world/discovery_w.py: a fork of discovery.Lineage with:
  * a W_CELLS mask on the discoverer's distribution and 64 candidates per step, with simulated values as the learner's fitness;
  * a generation of 16 steps, ending in a real confirmation of the best simulated candidate since the last one if its value is >= SIM_MARGIN;
  * the stratified 16-seed gate, acceptance and refit;
  * records w_step, w_accept, w_refit and w_lineage_done.
* rsi6/world/experiment_w.py: stages world, discovery, selection, swap_sim and heldout, with design o's replay-from-ledger rules.
* rsi6/registry/registration_w.json.
* rsi6/tests/test_world.py.

Constants:
* TABLE_THETA 4000, TABLE_PROBLEMS 20 (fewer if a pool is smaller), K_NN 3.
* SIM_TASKS 48, CANDIDATES 64, GEN_STEPS 16.
* SIM_MARGIN: the simulated value that the D4 calibration maps to +0.004 real.
* GATE_SEEDS 16, GATE_Z 2.33, GATE_MEAN 0.004.
* CPU_STEP 1.10, CPU_RATIO 1.25.
* REFIT_RADIUS: the 90th percentile of the nearest-neighbour distances of generation 0's own trajectories.
* REFIT_MAX 500 per category per adoption.

What it gives up: no representation discovery. score/pick edits, theta/grow and shortlist are outside the W cells because they would invalidate the table.
measurement_design:
**Categories.**
* Discovery and the simulator use four source categories: quadratic assignment, job shop, p-median and bin packing. Knapsack is dropped because its acquired score is the same for every mechanism; partitioning and set covering are excluded for cost. Tables use the training pools only.
* Held-out: single-machine weighted tardiness, UBQP, RCPSP and maximum clique, touched only in the held-out stage.

**Arms.** Two lineages each, 12,000 CPU-s per lineage, interleaved, with design o's random-stream, tie and replay rules; every lineage starts at generation 0 of design o.
* W-rec.
* W-frozen.
* W-static.
* W-shuffled.
* R (real-only): design-o steps on the same W cells with real screening, and the same gate.

**Gate.** Each confirmation uses 16 new seeds per lineage (confirm_base + 1000 x lineage index + 16k + j), on part A, paired with the parent. Acceptance needs a stratified mean >= 0.004, z >= 2.33, CPU within 1.10 x the parent's and 1.25 x generation 0's.

**Selection.** Every lineage's final on part B with 6 seeds; the better lineage is the arm's final.

**Swap (simulator).** Runs only if W-rec's final has a live principle other than generation 0's: 24 paired replicate lineages of 300 CPU-s from generation 0, discoverer principle from W-rec's final vs from generation 0. Each replicate's best is scored on the independent table, and the top 3 pairs are checked by real runs on part B with 8 seeds.

**Held-out.** 24 new seeds, the registered run budget, empty memory.
* Arms: the W-rec, W-frozen, W-static, W-shuffled and R finals; retain-theta (generation 0 with its starting constants replaced by the table theta that is best on average over the four source tables: it keeps a skill and cannot change acquisition); o0; a0.
* Controls raised to W-rec's CPU pair by pair (evaluate.raise_until): o0@, a0@, W-frozen@, W-static@, R@, retain-theta@.
* W-rec's accepted generations, each at the registered budget, and the other lineage of every arm.
* Registered order under a 100,000 CPU-s cap: W-rec, o0@, W-frozen@, W-static@, R@, a0@, retain-theta@, then the rest. A binding cap drops secondary arms only.

**Statistic.** Fixed-category paired mean, seeds resampled within category (5,000 draws). Reported beside it: the sign of every category; acquired, untrained and gain; registration_o's category-resampled statistic.

**Endpoints.**
* H1: W-rec - o0@ >= 0.01, lower bound > 0, no category below -0.005, not void.
* H2: W-rec - W-frozen@ > 0 and W-rec - W-static@ > 0 (point estimates), not void.
* S1: swap mean > 0 with a 95% interval excluding 0, and at least 2 of 3 real checks positive.
* H3: Spearman between simulated value and real confirmed mean, over all W confirmations, >= 0.3.
* N: W-shuffled accepts nothing, and W-shuffled - o0@ has an interval that includes 0.
* E: W-rec adopted a mechanism whose live principle differs from generation 0's, and its selected final has one.

**Success.** Recursive improvement of discovery is reported as observed only if E, H1, H2, S1, H3 and N all hold.

**Partial answers named in advance.**
* W arms accept more than R at equal CPU: the self-model improves discovery on source categories (first order).
* S1 alone: recursion inside the self-model only.
* H1 alone: a better acquisition principle, without evidence of recursion.
* Nothing: a negative answer, with the limit identified by D3 and D4.
predictions: D2 (development, a gate for registering): surrogate rank fidelity >= 0.6 on 3 of 4 source categories; expected 0.7. This is the Spearman of k-NN against real per-problem keys over 200 theta proposed by real principles.

D4 (development, a gate for registering): Spearman between simulated value and real paired difference over 24 random W-cell mechanisms (4 categories x 6 development seeds) >= 0.3; expected 0.4. Below 0.3 the technique is not registered, and the negative is recorded.

D3 (development): the oracle gap (the best table theta's proxy gain minus generation 0's simulated gain) is at least 0.01 relative cost on 3 of 4 categories; expected yes on QAP, job shop and bin packing, not on p-median.
R1: W-rec adopts at least 1 mechanism in each of its 2 lineages; expected 1.5 adoptions per lineage, P(both) about 0.5.
R2: W-shuffled adopts nothing; expected 0 (about 10% chance of at least 1 false acceptance over about 10 confirmations).
R3: W-rec, W-frozen and W-static together adopt more than R at equal CPU; expected about 4 against 0 to 1.
R4 (H3): Spearman between simulated value and real confirmed mean over all W confirmations (about 30) >= 0.3; expected 0.35.
R5: adopted mechanisms average about +0.008 on their confirmation seeds and about +0.005 on part B selection seeds, much less shrinkage than design o's +0.0089 to +0.0012.
R6 (H1): not met. W-rec final - o0@matched on held-out: point +0.003, 80% interval -0.004 to +0.010; P(H1 met) about 0.2.
R7 (H2): W-rec - W-frozen@matched on held-out within +/-0.005, or not exercised (no adopted principle change); P(not exercised) about 0.35.
R8 (S1): if exercised, the mean simulated difference (discovered principle minus generation 0's as discoverer) is positive, but its interval includes 0; P(interval excludes 0 positively) about 0.3.
R9: refit helps. In confirmations from generation 3 on, W-rec's Spearman between simulated and real is higher than W-static's by about 0.1 (underpowered, reported only).
R10: E holds (W-rec's selected final has another live principle): P about 0.55.

R11: overall, the success condition is not met (P about 0.9). The most likely outcome is a first-order partial result: W arms adopt real source-category improvements that R does not, and nothing on held-out at 0.01.
failure_modes: Low fidelity: the k-NN table misranks principles (sparse 10-dimensional coverage, or principles that exploit table gaps with large steps). Simulated winners are then no better than random edits (mean -0.002) and only false acceptances occur. Detected by D2, D4 and H3; mitigated, not removed, by refits.
The internal proxy ignores test-time local improvement. A principle that builds better constructions can leave the kernel's acquired score unchanged after local improvement, which would cap fidelity.
Small oracle gap: generation 0's fixed linear policy saturates, so no principle can gain much. That is a negative answer that names the fixed representation, not the principle, as the limit (D3).

Source specificity: the four source landscapes (about 20 problems each, QAP dominating the variance) select principles fitted to their geometry. Held-out shows a null, as the earlier processes did (cross-category correlation about 0).
Held-out categories may have flat acquisition, as p-median and knapsack do here: any principle scores 0 there, and the 0.01 mean becomes unreachable.

Self-application may not transfer across levels. A principle tuned for 5-8 rounds of 10-dimensional theta search may learn the discoverer's weights over about 25 cells and about 80 steps worse than generation 0's does, making W-rec worse than W-frozen; this is reported as such.
The recursion is not exercised: no principle change is adopted (P about 0.35), so H2 and S1 are empty.

Costs above estimates: bin packing constructions or simulation CPU above about 1 s per candidate. CANDIDATES drops to 32 by a registered rule, with fewer steps; the per-run cost of the held-out categories is unknown, which is why the held-out cap and arm order are registered.
Matched controls that do not reach the arm's CPU void their comparisons (registration_o's rule).
novelty:
**Relative to design o.** The edit space is the same but restricted to what keeps the score and pick programs fixed, so there is no representation discovery. The discoverer is the same, and so is the self-application of the parent's principle to the discoverer's weights. What is new is the evaluator: a recorded model of the learner's own acquisition landscape. A learning principle is run inside it instead of being measured by kernel runs, and the model is refit by the behaviour of each adopted principle. Also new is the stronger gate this makes affordable: 64 pairs, threshold 0.0065.

**Relative to design q.** Design q moved program search inside acquisition, under the meter, where it starved (5-8 rounds, 4-problem batches, -0.002 against o0). Here the search over principles happens outside acquisition, on recorded constructions, and only real kernel runs adopt.

**Relative to known algorithms.** This is surrogate-assisted evolutionary search and meta-black-box optimisation (learning optimisers on cheap surrogate tasks, as with learned evolution strategies), with active refitting of the surrogate. It is close in spirit to the Owner's reference of instruction 4: predict the effect of a modification before making it. It is not a fundamentally new computational principle and not more radical than design o. It gives up novelty of the search space in exchange for power: design o's recursion gets exercised at every step and becomes measurable at all. It does not answer the question that this angle asked for something radical in order to answer.
implementation_plan:
Day 1, about 1,100 lines, no change to any pinned file.

1. rsi6/world/landscape.py (about 180 lines) with tests. No reference is read: env.score and env.reference are monkeypatched to raise during record and refit. The kernel's fresh ids (parts A and B) never enter a table. Block-normalised lookups are exact for points in the table.
2. rsi6/world/simulator.py (about 220 lines) with a replay-equivalence test. During a real _acquire_open run on a source fixture, record every (theta, problem) key by wrapping construct, and build a table from them. Simulating the same mechanism and seed must then reproduce the iterations, the chosen theta and the held-back fitness exactly.
3. rsi6/world/discovery_w.py (about 260 lines, a fork of discovery.Lineage with the W_CELLS mask, simulated values, generations, the stratified gate and refit).
4. rsi6/world/experiment_w.py (about 260 lines; stages world, discovery, selection, swap_sim, heldout; registration and file pins checked as in experiment.py).
5. rsi6/registry/registration_w.json and rsi6/tests/test_world.py (about 150 lines).

Development checks, on source categories only, on a scratch ledger with development seeds, all before registration:
* D1: replay equivalence.
* D2: surrogate rank fidelity, using 200 principle-proposed theta per category constructed for real.
* D3: oracle gap from the tables.
* D4: sim-to-real calibration. 24 mechanisms (generation 0 plus 23 random 1-3-edit W-cell mechanisms) in the kernel on 4 categories x 6 seeds (part A) and in the simulator. Gives the Spearman, SIM_MARGIN, and an estimate of the sd of real effects among W-cell edits (resolvable down to about 0.005).
* D5: null calibration of the 16-seed stratified gate with registration_o's noise stub; expected at most 1% per confirmation.
* D6: end-to-end run with the CPU budgets divided by 20, including a stage stopped and resumed.
* Measured CPU per construction and per simulated candidate, which fixes CANDIDATES.

Rule: if D2 or D4 fails, nothing is registered, the measured negative is reported, and the technique stops there.
compute_budget:
**Development:** before registration, on source categories, not part of the 300,000; about 18,000 CPU-s.
* Development tables, 1,000 theta x 20 problems x 4 categories: about 2,000.
* D2: about 500.
* D4: 25 mechanisms x 6 seeds x about 51 CPU-s per mechanism-seed (sum of the four categories): about 7,700.
* D5 stub: about 100.
* D6 at budgets divided by 20: about 6,000.
* Timing: about 200.

**Registered experiment** (cap 260,000 of 300,000):

| Stage | CPU-s |
|---|---|
| World: 4,000 theta x 20 problems x 4 categories, plus the independent 20-problem table for the swap (bin packing about 70% of it) | about 12,000 |
| Discovery: 5 arms x 2 lineages x 12,000 | 120,000 |
| Selection: 10 finals plus o0, 6 seeds x about 51 CPU-s | about 3,400 |
| Swap: 24 pairs x 2 x 300 simulated, plus a real check of 3 pairs x 2 x 8 seeds | about 14,400 + 2,500 |
| Held-out (4 categories x 24 seeds, about 12 CPU-s per run assumed) | about 35,000 expected, cap 100,000 |
| **Expected total** | **about 187,000** |

* One W lineage spends about 2,600 on simulation, about 5 confirmations x 1,630 and at most 1,500 on refits.
* Held-out breakdown: 8 arms at the registered budget about 9,200; W-rec trajectory and other lineages about 9,000; 6 matched controls at about 2.5 x the arm's CPU about 17,000.

About 73,000 CPU-s stays between the expected total and the cap, and about 40,000 beyond the cap within the 300,000, for raised-budget levels, replays and a held-out cost above 12 s per run.
